title: Authentication, scope authorization and caller attribution boundaries
purpose: Find reachable violations of established authentication and authorization contracts across registered HTTP routes, unary and streaming RPCs, per-element batch scopes, client versus internal trust and admission-time caller attribution. Apply the companion evidence and ownership contract. Preparation of this manifest does not authorize an audit: refresh the scope after the auth PRs stabilize and obtain a separate execution decision. Do not assume tenant or ledger-specific authorization, promote proposed refactors into current invariants, duplicate tracked credential disclosure causes, or expand into a general security audit.
invariants: Every hypothesis must identify an actually registered route or RPC, server mode, installed guards, credential state and downstream operation. Protected methods enforce their established granular scope requirements when authentication is enabled. Inventory unary and streaming methods separately, including request-dependent policies; a declared policy or helper test alone does not prove runtime enforcement. Public, internal and restore surfaces follow their own explicit contracts (companion contract A).

With authentication enabled, no bearer uses configured anonymous scopes; insufficient anonymous scopes deny as HTTP 401 or gRPC Unauthenticated, invalid bearer credentials deny as unauthenticated, and a valid bearer lacking required scopes denies as HTTP 403 or gRPC PermissionDenied. Preserve deliberate public bypasses, configured anonymous writes, auth-disabled behavior and the documented non-Bearer-as-absent classification. Do not infer tenant or ledger-name restrictions from granular scope names (contract B).

Accepted client JWTs must satisfy the established signature, expiry, issuer and configured static-key scope/god restrictions of the applicable trust path before granting privileges. Scope expansion must not manufacture authority outside that policy. Assess OIDC audience and static-key exceptions against the approved EN-1926 decision and its actual landed implementation; the known missing-audience cause and verification-source work are deduplication context, not new findings or a claim that the base already implements them (contract C).

HTTP bulk and gRPC Apply must enforce the required scope of every decodable batch element before handing the batch to business processing, including mixed scope classes and nested ledger Apply variants. Authentication-disabled and trusted gRPC peer paths retain their explicit exceptions. RequiredScopeForRequest's OpsWrite fallback for unknown/malformed variants is not unconditional rejection; authoritative validation still applies. Preserve the documented signature-error precedence for an opaque signed payload that cannot be peeked (contract D).

A client cannot obtain cluster-internal or system-actor trust from an unverified caller field. On service gRPC, only the configured nonempty matching cluster secret establishes the current internal fast path; a forwarded caller snapshot supplied by a non-internal connection is rejected. Raft interceptors and restore-mode service registration have separate trust contracts, and HTTP has no equivalent cluster-secret fast path (contract E).

Established authenticated caller identity, expanded scopes and god state must survive the actual local or forwarded mutation path into the admission-time snapshot. System actors remain server-originated; trusted forwards retain the original attribution under the documented precedence. Snapshot data records attribution and must not be used to re-derive authorization. Do not require a non-nil principal for every current proposal: anonymous and auth-disabled caller-less states and stronger EN-1955 admission guarantees must be distinguished from lost authenticated context (contract F).

The resolved caller snapshot is frozen for committed execution: later token expiration or node-local authentication configuration must not change FSM authorization, applied effects or interpretation of that attribution. The audit chain's binding of caller data is an evidence boundary, not permission to audit all hashing, storage or restore mechanics. Follow only enough of proposal capture to establish an attribution failure or disprove one (contract G).
adversarial_questions: Which HTTP method/path and unary/streaming RPC pairs are registered in normal, Raft and restore modes at this SHA? Which exact public exceptions exist, and do actual installed middleware/interceptors or handler checks enforce the stated policy before protected work or stream output? Recount descriptors instead of copying historical method counts.

Can a dynamic GetIndex, GetIndexEntryStatus or ListIndexes target select a different scope branch? Do HTTP facade, RPC and corresponding Apply variant agree where the repository requires that agreement? Are independently installed stream guards exercised, including any first-message policy after future refactors land?

For absent, non-Bearer, empty Bearer, malformed, expired, wrong-issuer, invalid-signature and valid-insufficient-scope credentials, which guard runs and what exact status and downstream-call count result? Which public paths bypass credential validation even with an invalid bearer, and which merely require no scopes?

Can virtual scopes, wildcard expansion, unknown scopes, a missing anonymous mapping or a configured static-key allowlist accidentally yield greater authority? Is god mode admitted only under the applicable verified key policy? Do not invent new JWT claim requirements such as mandatory subject, nbf or token type without an established contract.

After refreshing EN-1926, does issuer/audience enforcement follow the successfully verified trust source, including OIDC Ed25519 signatures and distinct static/OIDC keys sharing a kid? Are matching string/array audiences, missing/wrong audiences and the static-key exemption evaluated according to the landed contract? Is a suspected failure already the tracked cause or a distinct remaining mechanism?

Can a first authorized batch element hide a later unauthorized element, or a nested Request variant escape the scope mapping? Exercise anonymous-empty, anonymous-write, restricted bearer, auth-disabled and trusted-forward states. Does malformed signed input still reach signature validation in the intended order rather than becoming evidence of a scope bypass solely because PeekBatch failed?

Can a forged forwarded_caller_snapshot cross the external gRPC boundary with no secret, a wrong secret, an ordinary valid JWT or auth disabled? Conversely, does a correctly trusted follower forward preserve the original caller? A trusted peer without a snapshot is an EN-1955 design/deduplication case unless a distinct established contract is violated.

For every currently present audited mutation entry point, is the context returned by authentication actually passed to forwarding/admission? Check dedicated mutation RPC removal in EN-1954 and the merged EN-1950 repair before naming a defect. Are server-originated system actors distinguishable from client-controlled input?

Can local claims override the trusted original snapshot, can the transport peer replace the business caller, or can a later mutation of shared snapshot data change the admitted attribution? Trace the real caller and capture order; a helper-manufactured context is not a wire-level exploit.

Does any downstream decision re-evaluate token validity or node-local auth state after admission? Distinguish caller attribution loss here from independent audit encoding, replay or restore defects owned by persistence/checker domains.

Does a proposed disclosure claim require changing an authorization decision, or is it the known public credential projection work in EN-1632/1634/1635? Route redaction, storage and driver causes to their existing owners; read access to sensitive-looking data alone does not establish an undocumented access-control rule.
dynamic_checks_to_consider: These are optional diagnostics for a separately authorized later audit. Use existing tests and allowed temporary diagnostics with the pinned Nix/native validation environment, synthetic keys/tokens and disposable local fixtures. Do not edit tracked files, implement reproducer patches, probe deployed services, expose real credentials, or invoke audit/challenge/Jira orchestration from a leaf provider. Report executed checks separately from reproduction plans.

Use HTTP route_scope_exhaustiveness_test.go, handlers_bulk_test.go and auth/http_middleware_test.go as seeds. Send requests through the registered router with valid non-auth inputs, capturing controller call counts and exact 401/403/allowed responses. Pair each denied case with a valid authorized control so an unrelated missing ledger or malformed body cannot satisfy the assertion.

Use server_bucket_auth_test.go, server_mutation_auth_context_test.go, server_bucket_test.go and client_bucket_test.go for per-element decisions and caller propagation. Verify the real service registration and protocol revision as well as handler behavior. For streams, observe the first Recv and terminal status plus protected backend entry; helper authorization success alone cannot prove the installed stream path.

Run existing request_scope_exhaustiveness_test.go and route_scope_exhaustiveness_test.go against all current oneofs/routes. Construct mixed permitted/denied batches with the denied item at different positions and nested ledger actions; assert no business dispatch after a denied scope. Keep malformed signed-payload signature precedence as a separate observation.

Use grpc_auth_test.go, scopes_test.go, ed25519_keys_test.go and composite_keyset_test.go fixtures for verified signatures, expiry, issuer, scope expansion and god-key restrictions. Resolve the pinned go-libs dependency when following JWT verification. Use a local fake issuer/JWKS for OIDC tests; only run post-EN-1926 audience scenarios against the refreshed implementation and record absent coverage honestly.

Use caller_snapshot_test.go and the actual client/server forwarding fixtures to compare subject/source, sorted scopes and god state before and after forwarding/admission. Cover trusted and spoofed snapshots, absent attribution, explicit system components and auth-disabled/anonymous modes independently. Synthetic in-process markers must not stand in for proof that an external caller can set them.

Use raft_auth_test.go and bootstrap registration evidence to distinguish Raft unary/stream protection from client JWT authentication. Check health policy separately for each server plane: configured Raft authentication also protects its health RPCs; service health/protocol exemptions do not imply a Raft exemption. Inspect restore's binding and service set without executing destructive restore RPCs. No real cluster secret rotation, operator rollout or live identity-provider traffic is authorized by this manifest.
